Mrillis Action!, is a screen recorder that gives you high quality videos and a stylish, easy to use interface. The layout is simple and easy to use, while still having everything you would want in a screen recorder. It has 3 modes: "Gaming mode", which, as the title would suggest, is best for recording gaming videos. "Active Screen" or "Windowed mode" which records your entire desktop screen, unlike Gaming Mode which only records the game window. And then "Active Desktop Region." This mode is mainly used if you want to target and record a specific area on your screen.
This screen recorder also has built in audio recording and snapshotting abilities, which can come in handy.
This screen recorder isn't perfect, so let's get into some of its cons.
1. Sometimes while trying to record a specific game, (Minecraft for instance) the big red "record" button is greyed out and you are unable to click on it. So you are forced to just use the hotkey "F9" to start and stop the recording. However, this can become tedious, at least for me. I for one have had a few experiences where I accidently pressed the wrong button and I didn't record. And although a lot of people don't think being forced to use the hotkey is a bad thing, I personally wish I could press the button instead for certain situations. I'm not sure if this is for all games or not, but this has happened for quite a few games before.
2. Sometimes the start and stop recording hotkey is unresponsive. Often when you start a recording then stop it, then start it again, it won't start the second time and you are left talking to yourself in your house and you gained no recording. Its really a let down when you have been recording for an hour and then you look back and it hasn't been recording at all. This is another reason I wish I could just press the red button to start the recordings and that it wasn't all greyed out for some reason.
3. If your game crashes while you are recording, that video file becomes corrupted and you cannot view it. This really blows and is one of the main reasons I stopped using bandicam and switched to Action, because bandicam did the same thing. However, it appears Action has the same problem. I really wish when the game crashed the recording would continue on, but be a black screen instead, or perhaps would just stop the recording. But instead if your game crashes you lose that recording, which is very dissapointing.
4. The price. I know this isn't exactly a strong con, but I should mention that this recorder costs $49.99. Not a terrible price to pay for a screen recorder, but still pretty expensive. I'd recommend waiting until there's a sale and pick it up for maybe $40 or $35.
And that's all I can really think of for cons at the moment.
So:
Cons:
1. Can't click the starting and stopping button on some games.
2. Start and stop recording hotkey is sometimes unresponsive.
3. If your game crashes while you are recording, you lose that recording.
4. Its a bit pricey.
Pros:
1. Stylish Interface that is easy to use while still providing all the necessary settings you would need for a screen recorder.
2. High quality videos.
3. Multiple recording options
4. Audio and snapshotting abilities.
5. Stable.
Overall I would definitely recommend this software, especially if you are a youtuber like myself. Its easy to use and really doesn't dissapoint too much. It has its problems, but personally I feel the pros outweigh the cons.
Its a very handy application that you should get even if you are not a youtuber. However, i'd advise picking it up during a sale.
Thanks for reading! :)

Spawning as a whole is my problem. The whole system is terrible. If an enemy is capturing your final objective, you can still spawn on it because, well, where else should you spawn you know? But your supposed to be protecting it when you spawn but this is very hard to do as the game decides to place you a mile away from the objective in an open field. At this point, many enemy tanks sit on a hill and shoot you as you spawn. And my least favorite spawn issue: When you spawn in, you have five seconds. Within these 5 seconds, you are both invisible and invincible. However, this invisibility breaks when you shoot. So im standing in a door way. I checked my corners and everything. Then a fresh spawn literally comes out of thin air and shoots me. I dont care if that person just died. It is impossible to stop yourself from dieing if the guy can literally be invisible.
Another issue is weapon inbalances. When I first started playing this game, i instantly was aware of grenade spammers. When you first get the game, you are givin 2 items, a rifle and grenades. you can hold 4 grenades. so im by myself and 1v1 ing someone and right before they die they chuck all grenades in every direction and it takes half a second to pull a grenade. Getting killed by one of these guys is like getting killed by a noob tube in call of duty. This can be fixed by increasing the cost of grenades to from 400-800 credits per throw. Otherwise, spamming is an issue. Underpowered weapons also exist. In the game, you can get a sniper from taking the bolt action weapons and applying a scope on it. either you can wait until your level 9, which most people dont have the patience with, or you can get the bolt action and level it up until you unlock the scope. Like i said, i get between 16-17 thousand per hour. The bolt action costs 92 thousand and the scopes cost 72 and 90 thousand. THis is a LOT of money. Not only the price, the scopes are the last things you unlock with the gun. The guns itself is complete garbage for all countries. Now when i first got the gun i was 3 shotting people. 3 SHOTS!!! thats like the first rifle, only slower. now, with a better damageing bullet i SOMTIMES 2 shot people. mostly 3 shot. The only thing keeping me with this gun in the fact that it will be great later on but until then, the gun is trash.
My final though is that the vehicles still have a lot of work. The problem really just boils down to the fact that any rock or pebble will cause you to either flip your vehcile or commit suicide becaues you "crashed."
Now this is just a list of the problems really, but the pros outweigh the cons. The game itself is amazing and I would easily recommend it to just about anyone. Just like every other game, this one has some problems.  But that shouldnt really be a problem. and 1 more thing. Everyone says this game is pay2win. ITS NOT! Pay2win implies that paying with real money gives you an advantage over people that didnt pay. really, the only thing paying does is decrease the time it takes to get stuff. I can get everything a payed player gets by just playing the game. Period.

The title itself is misleading. For those looking for a genuine realistic 'Surgeon Simulator'; then look elsewhere as the procedures come off as cartooney antics. Your average surgery involves smashing and ripping open a persons body without care and then plopping in a replacement organ or cutting  something out with brute force. While I am not personally annoyed by this, it would have been better had the developers chose a less serious title for the more wacky humor involved in the entire concept of the game.
The controls are a huge factor for many who have played the game.. You could rename this to: Re tarded Limp Hand Simulator 2013, as it's major turn off to really enjoying the game. Every interaction between the limp hand and an object usually comes off awkward. You'll never be able to properly hold something like a bonesaw unless its angled in a proper position. Nor will you be able to use it properly (sawing bone) as it has the same effect as the hammer, where you just destroy anything that is in front of you.
In short; if you're looking for a game based around surgery with a lot of depth, then I can't recommend it. There are other surgeon games that are vastly superior; one of them being the Trauma Center series found on the DS and Wii.
If you're looking for a tongue and cheek humor game that doesn't take itself seriously yet suffers from awkward controls, then you'll find some value out of it. However only buy it when it goes on sale.

As of 5/5/16, Parkitect has created the old spark that I had as a kid playing the old Roller Coaster Tycoon games (not #3). The game has kept that old-timey feel of locked rotation as well as giving the player the option to rotate the camera freely (to a point). I would recommend it in it's current state 100%. It's pretty decently polished, has the gameplay, and introduces community mods and blueprints to the steam workshop as well as ParkitectNexus.
The graphics in the game are very polished. While it has some glitches here and there, it is an alpha and I look passed that. Parkitect is very aesthetically pleasing in the way of color and presentation. Every time I go in to the game I enjoy looking at it becasue it's not too bright or boring (However, you do get the options to make it boring or very colorful).
8/10
Parkitect offers
in terms of gameplay. Right now there is no story mode or campaign. However, there is a Sandbox mode that lets the player pretty much do anything they would like. The game runs pretty smoothly, however in terms of performance, even on my R9 290x it bogs down in some of the bigger maps when zoomed out.
The game gives the player many options for customizations on things such as buildings, landscapes, people, etc. I love that the game gives players the option to follow around certain people and see what they're doing in your park. It helps quite a bit to see how to optimize your park, and where to do so.
*More to come as I get more in depth with the game. Limited time writing and such.

This game is by far my favorite game when it comes to just enjoyment while playing with friends. Fighting, driving, stealing, and just generally doing stupid stuff is a ton of fun in this game, but the way that Rockstar does business makes this game near unbearable sometimes.
First of all if you want to actually get anywhere in the game and you don't want to give up 1000+ hours of your life to the game you're going to absolutely have to buy a shark card at some point. They aren't super cheap either. $20 get's you something a little over $1 million. Which in this game doesn't get you far. Most high end sports cars are over a million, and the best car in the game will cost you something like $3 million fully upgraded.
That's not even going into DLC. The most recent gunrunning DLC is so insanely expensive that just to get all the vehicles it will cost you between $10,505,000 - $13,971,900. Yes that is 8 zeros... The bunker will cost you minimum $1,165,000 just to get started on the new mission content, and then when you go into your bunker the first time, if you haven't already bought the $3 Million - $4 Million dollar mobile operations unit, agent 14 will literally tell you that you should buy it. This game is built around huge amounts of money that are near impossible to obtain legitimately in a timely manner.
Here we get into the second problem I've found while playing this game. Hackers. They are everywhere. Teleporting, spawning vehicles, killing, and dropping money everywhere. Literally an hour ago I ran into a hacker teleporting on top of me and blowing me up every single time I spawned. The only way to stop it was to switch to passive and leave the server. Not to mention that despite the fact I actively avoided getting cheated money when I could, I received a notification upon downloading the new DLC "warning me" that I shouldn't cheat. Thanks! That's helpful! I'll remember that next time I'm teleported to the top of the Maze Bank tower and have literal bags of money dropped onto my head and then get blown up. I'll just do my best to use my will power to repel the hackers away. So if you're interested in getting this game I recommend you be prepared to be heavily under powered compared to everyone else unless you're willing to whale money into the game or grind for thousands of hours. Either that or you'll eventually succumb to the temptation of hacked money and just start begging in chat for someone to give you money like half of the people playing this game, thus risking getting banned and losing the money you payed for this full priced 4 year old game and any time and energy you spent playing the game.
Last but certainly not least we have the recent issue of OpenIV, an essential part of the GTAV modding community, receiving a Cease & Desist letter. This has basically put to a halt the whole modding community, which for some people was the only reason they got the game on PC in the first place. The single player isn't very fun to play and there are certain vehicles and bits of content that can't even be accessed in the single player without the use of mods. In effect Rockstar by getting rid of OpenIV, has forced players to go to online to get access to these things. I can't help but feel that the intent was to bring in more online players and in effect bring in more people spending money on cash cards to gain access to content that should easily be available in the single player mode, but isn't. While this is just my speculation I feel it is worthy of bringing up in my review of the game because for some who many be considering getting the game to try a mod they saw somewhere for single player they will now likely be unable to do so.
I would like to say this is in fact my favorite game and I will probably continue to play the game for a while to come, but these 3 big issues force me to leave a negative review as I can't in good conscience recommend a game that is actively trying to get money out of the player base and filled with unsportsmanlike cheating, while also taking out a modding community of people playing single player.

I know its a bit of a meme to compare difficult games to dark souls, but in my opinion this game really is similar.
Remember the feeling you had when you finally cleared that one boss that gave you so much trouble? That is every obstacle in this game. The relief and pride you feel after a particularly difficult part in the game is equivalent to finally beating ornstein and smough. This gives you just enough reason to continue playing and subjecting yourself to potentially mind breaking frustation, only for it to all be repayed with joy upon completion. This game is the most pure form of the primary difficulty-anger-completion-joy loop in many difficult games.
Another great mechanic in the game design is how it becomes more difficult the more frustated you get. As you continue to fail a part, your mouse movements become more erratic and imprecise, which only serves to make it more difficult, and possibly set you back even further. Once you realize this, it is much easier to progress and stay calm.
On top of these two main components of the game, the gameplay and game itself is fun and easy to pick up but difficult to master. The sound design is wonderful, with the occasional insightful quote after completing an obstacle, thematic music playing occasionally, hearing your character moan "Oh no" as you fall losing who knows how much progress, and the clangs of your hammer against the different materials permeates your soul.
In conclusion, this game is a new kind of experience that will challenge your will while teaching and making you a better person along the way if you can make it. If you give up, maybe you don't deserve it. Much like the real Hollows in Dark Souls are those who quit the game, permanently leaving their character in limbo, people who quit this game are losing to the developer; and who knows, maybe thats what he wanted all along.

TLDR: Game has good life lessons, fun gameplay, precise controls, and an overall good feel. Incredibly rewarding game if you are willing to challenge yourself.

I had hoped to modify this review to be more positive, but Rockstar Games has again take moves that are abjectly anti-consumer.
Rockstar has made "adjustments" to the in-game account balance of its players. THis is fine as an anti-cheat measure if:

Well, the game does speak for itself, mostly.
I like the fact it's an upgraded version of the old Rollercoaster Tycoons. Graphically it looks a lot better.
Also, there's modding; there are camera mods that let you ride your rides, or walk amongst your visitors.
There's a ton of scenery and it's really easy to lose track of time when building your own park.
This is THE sandbox mode we've always wanted in the old Rollercoaster Tycoons.
So, is it all good? No, not really... However, the not-so-great things are all down to this game still being in alpha.
My experience is completely based on the Alpha 9a, which was the version before the Steam EA version.
The game is rather demanding; I've installed the 9a version on my old PC (DualCore 2.6GHz, Radeon HD 7870, 4GB DDR3) for my girlfriend to play with. The game has to be put on lowest settings and still stutters when it's raining and she has more than 100 guests in her park. She doesn't mind, since she isn't a gamer and she's mostly looking at the pretty flowers ;) But it does show a lot of room for optimization - the patch notes did mention a lot of performance improvement in the latest patch, but I have no experience with that patch yet.
The game runs well on my own PC (FX-8150 (OC'd to 4GHz), R9 290 (Asus OC edition) and 8GB DDR3) at stable 60 FPS.
I still do recommend this game for the following reasons:
- if you liked the old RCTs, you'll definitely enjoy this as well.
- it's not expensive at 15 euro
- it's early access, so there's promise for a WHOLE lot more to come
- there's a rather active modding community

Disclaimer: At the time of writing this review, I have been playing a pre-alpha release for ~40h.
This game is a perfect modernisation of RollerCoasterTycoon2. If you don't care about realistic 3D graphics and riding your coasters, I guarantee you'll have more fun playing Parkitect, than RCTWorld or PlanetCoaster.
It really is a faithful succesor to RCT2. Most acpects of the game are designed to resemble the feel of classic RollerCoasterTycoon, but removing the limits and expanding on available options. The park building mechanisms are similar - yet more powerful and finer-grained. For example, you can divide the grid by 4 for finer precision when placing trees. Track slopes may have as much as 6 tilt levels in both directions. Ride entrances may be turned 90 degrees. The developers clearly are veterans of the classic game, and know very well what made the original so good, and what should be improved.
The modernized graphics style is unique - cartoon asthetics fit the theme perfectly. The game has a very HD feel to it, as the cartoonish style is minimalistic yet plesantly detailed.
There is a wire variety of attractions to build already in the game, but if that's not enough, the mod support is very solid.
And finally, the dev team keeps good contact with the community. There are very frequent updates and the progress done is amazing, they are also open to feedback and ideas.
Strongly recommended for all RCT veterans. For everyone else, you may want to wait a little more - the campaign mode and in-game economy are not yet implemented, and the bare sandbox mode may make the game confusing for newcommers.

(I reccomend, Gekokujo, L'aigle, Parrabellum, Perisno, and the Third Age)
-The learning curve for Mount and Blade is not too steep, but still offers a challenge. Think of it as easy to learn, hard to master.
-The diplomacy in the game is fleshed out enough that it is enjoyable, but not extended enough so that mods may take their own toll with the in game diplomacy.
-A lot of customization for you, as well as companions you meet within the game.
-Kingdoms vary a lot from each other, so playing experinces will be different from your last. An example being if you play as the Sarranids, you may use horse units a lot more, but if you play as the nords, archers become your friends.
-Online play offers variety as well as duels to test your skill against friends, bots or random opponets online.
The DLC (Napoleonic Wars) is totally worth the 10 dollars, and changes the game completely. This new DLC adds new gamemods such as Commander (Lead AI Troops against other players in the style of the Campaign), as well as line battles between online groups of regiments if thats what your into.
-The start game is really fun, and can really become a time consumer if your not careful.
(Though the game is relativly old, I still have to remark of the graphics).
-The graphics are good at best on ultra. The game is relativly old and this shows with how the faces look on people and how building's textures look within towns. If your looking for a good graphical game like Mount and Blade, wait for Mount and Blade: Bannerlord to realease, as it seems a lot better in its state of graphics.
-The endgame can become boring. After you have conquered the whole entireity of the game's large map (May take a while). The game seems to get boring, and repetative after you have completed everything. This can be fixed though with mods and different playing styles.
-Glitches in the game can overwhelm you if your not careful. Using mdos comes with its own risk, especially outside of the steam workshop. If you mash too many mods together, you may experience a pile of steaming garbage, being a waste of 20 dollars. So please tread at your own pace. Thankfully, most of the Glitches are not game breaking, and wont cause crashes.
-Unless you have a beast of a computer (Which I dont, I just wait through the lag) You will experince a lot of lag, especially in 150v150 battles, sieges or conversational screens (If both parties have more than 1800 troops at guess). This can be countered by lowering your graphics settings, or how many units on the field.Note that lowering your graphics settings will make your graphics experince a lot worse, and maybe at sometimes look downright ugly.
Certain features can be counted as good and bad.
-Unforgiving World: If you spend a lot of training a unit up from start to finish, so that they are the best unit in their class as well as faction, they still has the chance of dying and never coming back. You can lose all of your army, and sometimes a lot of your Denars (in game gold) because you lost a battle, got captured, or were ambushed. This gives a sense of challenge within the game, and can sometimes make you feel frustrated.
-Prejudiced AI: Starting the game as a woman can make your time and experince a lot harder, as women were not given the same rights of men during Medieval Times. This may or may not be a good experince for you. If you wish to have the hardest experience possible, starting out as a Women Farmer, is your best bet. Know that the Kings of the land will not see you as a rightful ruler, bescause of your sex. Marrying into a high ruling family can increase your changes of Stweardship, but this is very unlikely. This prejudice option can be turned off however.
-King Harlaus wont stop giving feasts: King Harlaus is the King of the in game Kingdom of Swadia. One flaw with him is the fact that he hosts feasts in the most strange and insane times. Feasts can be good, but may also distract you, as well as other AI Vassals, especially in a time of war. Feasts can be used to improve relations with other lords, talk to the King in Private, or look for a lady to marry/Husband to marry. But if I must attend another feast within the spand of 3 god damn minutes, I Will flip.
All In all, Mount and Blade is one fo my favorite games, and I do solely reccomend you buy it, especially if there is a sale on Taleworlds games.

Mobius Final Fantasy is a simple game that's ultimately completely average.
You load in as a "blank" in the world of Paramecia. A variety of people try to tell you what to do, but the story is so painfully thin that you'd be doing well if you even know why you're doing what you're doing. There's almost nothing for roleplaying and no choices of consequence, making this a purely action game.
Action-wise the game is not complicated. There's a big world map, and you move from one node to another. Within each node, there's a fight. The fight mechanics are very simple. There are four elements: wind <-> earth and fire <-> water. Each turn you generate some elemental orbs of the four elements, and you need these to perform attacks of the corresponding type. Attacks of each element are super effective against the opposite element and neutral against the other two. There's also an "element drive" option, where you use the orbs of an element to reduce the damage taken by attacks of that element. There are some other subtleties involved but it doesn't take a genius to see that you just use the attack that's super-effective, and use the other element to element drive. Perhaps that's why the game's autocombat system that's pretty decent, although it occasionally still does silly things.
So if there's no role-playing, the story is minimal and the action simple enough to get boring after a few hours, what's the point of playing the game? The only remaining factor is seeing your character get stronger and stronger. But even in this MFF is not particularly good: to level up your character and its attacks, you need to grind, but the game doesn't let you grind. See, each time you move a node on the world map, it consumes stamina. Stamina regenerates at a rate of one point every 5 minutes. Pretty soon you'll have no stamina left, and then you can't even play (without spending money anyway)!
If your spare time comes in blocks of a few minutes, then MFF is decent enough. You can log in, fight a few battles using autocalculate (which lets you do something else in the meantime as well), log back out. If you're looking for some kind of emotional engagement and challenge however, MFF falls very far short. I mark this as "not recommended" since I don't like to recommend games that aren't good to my friends; however it doesn't mean it's a bad game. If what you're looking for coincides with what it offers, it's OK, especially considering it's free.
Pros: Nice graphics; doesn't take up much time; smooth gameplay
Cons: Boring gameplay; no depth; actively encourages you not to play via the stamina mechanic
Rating: 5/10

Appendix, 06.07.16:
The new DLC is nice aswell. It delivers a few new items, stats, pets and dwarves. You don't need it but to be honest, the female dwarves are a nice addition.
Also, some of the visuals changed. The dwarves were reworked and have a new appearance. Even if not every update brings major changes, you can feel that this game is constantly under construction. You can always feel the progress. I never experienced any crashes or gamebreaking bugs. And I can't wait to see how the multiplayer will evolve. This game would be the greatest fun if two people could actually play one campaign.
Original review:
Craft The World is what it looks like. Its full of crafting, macro- and micro-management, lovely, survival and progression. At first, the game had some serious issues. Or lets say, the AI had its issues. But its constantly updated and you will feel that it gets better with every update.
The visuals look alot like any BigFishGames game. Its plain, but lovely.
The gameplay itself can be pretty addicting. Many people are annoyed by the techtree progression system, but if you do not like to use it, you can just play the game in sandbox mode. It will replace the techtree with recipes that you will find throughout the game. If you do not like this either, just open the wiki website, pretty much like in minecraft, and craft anything you want.
A pretty neat feature is that you can either give commands to your dwarfs or take over any of them and do the work yourself. That can be really helpful when it comes to crafting complicated structures. Or just sit back, relax and let the dwarfs do all the work.
The AI, as mentioned, sometimes struggles from pathfinding problems and such. But there are many ways to get around those problems.
(Sidenote: I constantly killed giants in Skyrim by simply running around an obstacle and shooting lightings at them while they were too dumb to figure out how to get to me.) There is NO perfect AI in any game. But at least the devs in CTW always try to improve your precious minions.
A few weeks ago, they launched the multiplayer mode. Right now, you have to unlock this mode. You need a certain amount of dwarfs, but thats not bad. It just means, you have to advance a little in singleplayer and than can join multiplayer matches. There are pvp or coop matches. You will join a new biome and have to beat the main boss. But first, you have to dig, collect and craft. Its really nice and the unique rewards will help you improve your main biome. The only sad thing about the multiplayer is that there is no way to start right off with a friend and play on the same map ... yet.
I was truly amused when I first found a Jason mask that can be worn by the dwarfs. So, its clearly visible that the devs keep adding fresh content. For an early access game, it is very stable!
If you're into management, crafting without being the active part in the game, you should give it a try. And hey: There are no freaking micro-transactions in this game. Only micro-management.

I supported this game on Kickstarter two years ago and have watched it grow from a pre-alpha version to the wonderful coaster sandbox it is now. The low-poly graphics are light on your system so you can simulate huge parks with more guests and staff. With over a dozen coaster types to play with; plenty of shops, 'flat rides', decor, and terraforming you can design the park you want.
Coaster games at their core are business simulation managers and Parkitect does that better than the rest by allowing you to focus on that aspect rather than high resolution graphics. The game has been updated frequently before release on Steam and the developers are continuing to update the game. Overall Parkitect is the best coaster game out there if you want to build gigantic parks.

Let me begin with, I was one of the individuals who contributed to the Kickstarter to help this game become a reality. Heck, I remember when Sebastian was showing off his concept work using programmer art to demonstrate the systems he was working on. Then Garret hopped on the train and the game REALLY took off. I would liken this game to a beautiful fusion of the original Theme Park by Bullfrog and RollerCoaster Tycoon 2. I will explain the how and why later on in my review. This game as a whole is a massive labor of love by everyone involved and it truly shines because of this.
Gameplay:
The game plays exactly how you would expect a Theme Park simulator to play. You paint paths, place rides and shops, build coasters of doom- I uh mean Thrilling Coasters!1!!1, and hire staff for your park. On top of that you also are in charge of planting scenery, constructing buildings, terra-forming, adding water to your park, and so much more! If you have played RollerCoaster Tycoon then a lot of this will feel very similar and you can easily dive in with a few quirks. A feature in Parkitect that the RollerCoaster Tycoon games lack is a shopkeeper and stock system. This was present in Bullfrogs Theme Park in the form of a graph like GUI where you order stock for your burger shop or drink stall through delivery trucks. In Parkitect you hire "Haulers" who are staff members that will exit the park to pickup crates and deliver them to their respective stalls. This adds an additional layer of strategy on the game because you can either have your Haulers carry boxes through your park in plain sight or you have the option of constructing employee only paths that can hide behind the scenes or travel underground! To top this off the Staff Paths can also lead to a building I wish we had in the RollerCoaster Tycoon series, a staff room! Without a Staff Room your Staff members will instead use the benches in your park, this will also contribute to them becoming more irritable as well.
The game also features a Piece by Piece building mode akin to what was available in RollerCoaster Tycoon 2. Speaking of building things, Parkitect removes the grid that everything was constrained to back in the day. With a caveat though, everything besides scenery is constrained to a grid. However trees and scenery pieces are free game during placement. An on demand grid with adjustable sizes is also avaiable with the ALT key if you prefer to precision place your objects. Also when it comes to track ride construction they added a lot of fantastic additions to make it feel familiar yet very powerful. It's still a Piece By Piece builder akin to RollerCoaster Tycoon, however they added fine tuning controls which are total game changers. You can now adjust the exact size of your piece by click on a "+" or "-" button to make them longer or wider. Mix that with the pitch controller (which lets you do a full 360 degree roll vs just 1 banking option like in RCT2) and you can create some extremely wide and twisted track designs. The game does a great job in giving you a very guided yet free form building environment.
In terms of Park Guests they are an absolute joy to amuse and please. ( I won't go into too much detail here as I have a lot to say about them in later topics). They explore your park as singular entities Ala RCT1 and 2 and go about their business carrying balloons, park maps, food, umbrellas, riding rides, vomitting, and ETC. For the sadistic players you are able to drop peeps into water and watch them suffer. :( Coasters can be derailed and crashed as well. The insanity continues!
Graphics:
The visuals in the game are downright gorgeous and adorable. The game sports a very toybox look which is both clean and aesthetically pleasing to the eye. While the games graphics are very simplistic don't let that fool you. Every object is chock full of detail, especially the rides and rollercoasters. You can see bolts, wheel assemblies, and ultra smooth animations on everything that moves. Flat rides are clean and distinctive with a full RGB color scheme to paint them with. The animations are wonderfully done with heavy pendulums showing clear stress from weight and Launched Freefalls giving me the sensation of weightlessness.
Coming back to the topic of people, they are very well done with a variety of skin tones, hair color and styles, and various accessories they wear such as backpacks and hats. Their animations are a joy to witness. All of their animations are extremely smooth with virtually no transition between them. What I mean is when a peep goes to sit down on a bench, they don't instally teleport to the seat. They actually turn around and will sit down, and do the same when standing up. This applies to everything such as benches and rides. Even food objects are smoothly eaten and disposed of. Their facial expressions are especially endearing as they animate on the fly and clearly demonstrate their emotion.
The game also allows the scenery objects to be scaled to different sizes and some can even have an adjusted color scheme. Trees sway in the wind, placing objects will cause a force that will push trees using a faux wind effect, and objects plop down and appear with satisfying animations. Buildings have a definite toylike look to them (which isn't a bad thing) and really compliment the colorful nature of the game. Water in the game is simplistic but gets the job done as well.
Sound:
The sound effects in the game absolutey elevate the experience even further. I don't even know where to begin as audio is a big focal point for me when playing games. Let's begin with the peeps. The general peep ambiance is very Sim Golf esque where there is a lot of audible gibberish and general blabber. It's quite entertaining to listen to and it definitely brought a smile to my face. On rides peeps scream and laugh very realistically. There is a lot of charm in this area because it ties everything together perfectly.
Rides creak, groan, and make very nice pneumatic sound effects. Shoulder harnesses and lap bars also make very nice clicking sounds and they're lowered and gates will squeak as they open and close. Rides also make satisfying clanks and clangs as they come to a stop or switch operating modes. Scenery also has a variety of sound effects as well. Trees make a nice planting sound, rocks clunk down on the environment, and flowers make a nice swoosh sound when planted. I think my favorite sounds have to be the ones objects and rides make when being placed. It's a very brassy, heavy, clank and clunk sound that definitely gives the illusion of the object having weight. I think Gordon, their sound designer did a phenominal job in this area.
Closing thoughts:
All in all this game has an incredible foundation setup for it. The developers did an incredible job keeping fans and prospective fans in the loop. They post weekly updates to their Tumblr, ar every active on Twitter, and occassionally do live streams showing the creation of new assets. They are also very receptive to modding, in which Parkitect Nexus will be your primary stop for everything Parkitect related (also run by incredible people). At this price you are getting a very solid experience with a lot going for it. I'm ecstatic to see where the future of the game goes from here. It has changed so much from the beginning but in the best ways possible.
TLDR;
This game is freakin amazing! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

I have been following Parkitect for some time now and was eagerly awaiting the business simulation games release on Steam before I purchased it.
Parkitect is reminiscent of the classic Rollercoaster Tycoon titles, right down to the isometric view and world charm.  In Parkitect, you must build a theme park from the ground up while managing finances, stock and staff.  Personally, this has been one of the most engrossing parts of the gamel; finding new ways to manage and balance finances.  For example, will guests come to your park if you charge a $30 entry fee with all rides at $0.30?  Damn right they will!
The main focus, however is on designing and creating a theme park from scratch.  You will be given a very substantial plot of land and a large amount of cash to get your park off the ground.  From here, you must entice guests to come to Mr. Fun's Funpark of Fun and spend all of their hard earned cash by pulling it from their cold dead hands in any way possible.  People need to pee, right?  Charge for toilet usage!
This game also gives you the ability to build rollercoasters' piece by piece that gives you the power to create the rollercoaster of your dreams, before charging out the♥♥♥♥♥for it.
The overall look, feel and charm of Parkitect is much like that of RollerCoaster Tycoon. Guests feel like they are experiencing your creations first hand. The ride music and ambience of chattering guests and rattling coasters make sure that your theme park comes to life.
Parkitect seemingly has modding built in it from the ground up, with the game featuring a modding menu and steam workshop integration that is akin to that of Cities: Skylines where players have the ability to create and upload their creations to the Steam Workshop for other business-savy players to make use of.  For example, I was in-game and placed a small eco park right in to the centre of my buzzing theme park.  Simple as that.  I believe that the type of modding integration available in Parkitect will vastly increase the games' longevity.
Right now the only game mode is a sandbox mode where all rides, shops, utilities, paths, etc are unlocked from the get go.  Hopefully in the future, we may see challenge modes or game modes where everything is not unlocked from the beginning.

Happened upon the sale here after playing the demo for a bit - for the current price (about the price of a beverage) it's totally worth it. It has really nice pixel art and excellent music which combine for a charming overall experience.

The gameplay also isn't quite the usual infinite runner - it's actually more like an evasion platformer, since you can run backwards and jump onto platforms and over enemies.

Currently the big goal is getting 20000 to unlock the next level - I'm not sure if there are other levels beyond that, but hopefully so, as it seems the game may loose steam if that's all there is to it. Either way it seems like the dev will probably keep working on the game so here are some ideas on what could be added (hereby free for the devs to use as they wish):

Weather - it seems a little too nice and sunny for proper Eastern Europe - sudden rain, hail or even snow could liven up the landscape and change the gameplay a bit (like making you slide).

Obstacles - there could be more variety here, with additional effects - here are some ideas: Golddigger girlfriend that clings onto you slowing you down (and sapping away money?) - tap jump to escape. Rival gang members - static obstacles that your posse can take care of (or possibly you as well with a well timed jump for a cash bonus). SWAT guys that your posse cannot stop. Grocery shop queue - just slows everyone down.

Powerups - what's there is fun, but there's room for more: Bicycle - faster movement, but smashing into obstacles is much more risky as it slows you down more. Skateboard - also faster movement, but smashing into obstacles makes you fall (your choice if that's deadly or can be recovered from). Moped - fastest movement, smashing into obstacles slows you down, smashing into wall/pipe is deadly.

Variety - it would be cool to run through different districts with different looks and obstacles - like slums, shopping district, industrial district etc. Entering a building or running down into a crossing tunnel (with pee puddles as obstacles) could also be neat.

So overally a neat little game. Hopefully the dev keeps up the good work and continues working on it.

Don’t Tax Me Bro:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
It’s tax time people, and just like you, I am ecstatic about it!  What a joy to give part of my well-earned money to the tax department. We have known about it since it was first introduced in the . . . what year was it? . . . not so long ago, around 3000 – 2800 BC in ancient Egypt. Anyway, from that time onwards, there have been people who don’t want to share their income with the tax department, and today, I DON’T WANT TO SHARE . . . Don’t Tax me Bro!
Don’t Tax me Bro is an endless platformer (until you get caught) where you take control of a dude who has no intention of paying his tax.
The point will be well established after two policemen slam your apartment door and run into the middle of your lounge room, shouting. . . HALT! What would  be your reaction? I’ll tell you straight, you’ll run out the window with the love of your life, (which is your briefcase full of $$$)!
From here it’s all about running faster than the cops, picking up additional coins and avoiding obstacles. Talking about obstacles, running onto people will slow you down, as will outdoor cafe/restaurant settings. And that’s just the start of it! What about those cats who are sitting on the window sill and wiggling their tails around on those light flower pots. Yes, that’s right - pots are going to drop down left, right and centre! Still thinking about avoiding tax? Hang on, what about pavement works? Holes on the footpath and furious dogs too - avoid them! But what reall what gets me is the birds; no matter what, they’ll get you back! Jump too high and crows will hit your face and knock you out.
In this ordeal, you will have a couple of power-ups at your disposal. Well, that is if you can reach them. Pick up a coffee cup and you’ll run as fast as a jaguar; pick up a vacuum cleaner and suck up as many coins as you can; or the best one - pick up the phone and get your body guard to help you out for a short period of time.

Do you have any second thoughts about tax evasion? Well, in Don’t Tax Me Bro, you’re going to be caught anyway; the question is, how much money can you collect and how far can you go beforehand ?  The mechanisms of the game are simple, but it’s not as easy as you might think.
Nice pixel graphics and the soundtrack is pretty good, too. In terms of the controls, they are pretty responsive but I personally prefer using the gamepad. You can play on a local multiplayer, too, which is great fun. I personally would have liked to have more levels (there are only two at this stage).
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Nice Pixel artwork
-	Fun, fast and easy to play
-	Achievements & trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Needs more levels
-	Repetitive
Don’t Tax Me Bro is a fun casual game which you can play over and over again.
7/10

That being said, there's something about the game that makes you want to keep playing. You also feel invested in what's going on, and I think if I had to use one word to descibe this game, it would be 'feel'. The game does make you feel, and that's why I said I somewhat hated it. If you're looking for a quick game to play, get Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons. It works best with a controller, but can be played with a keyboard. The gist of it is that you control two brothers simultaneously to solve puzzles and complete action sequences. It gets awfully clever on you, and there are only very minimal cues in the game. That is, it rarely tells you what buttons you need to press. In fact, you've only got the movement controls for each brother and a button to make each of them separately interact with stuff in the environment. There's dialogue but it's audible only in gibberish and only serves to convey character emotion and build on the personalities of the cast. Through the journey you come to know the characters by the quirky way you control them, i.e. you'll probably end up paying more attention to one brother, while the other larks off in some other direction (keeping track of two characters at once is deceptively difficult.)
It's only a few hours long, but the price is right. It's almost criminal that during the last steam sale I was able to get it for something like $2.50. Normal price $15, it's actually on sale for $7.50 right now. Get it.

Surgeon Simulator 2013 almost falls into the category of "so bad it's good." You play as a disembodied arm and are tasked to cut some bones, pull out some organs, and plop a replacement organ back in. It suffices to say that the word "simulator" in the title is meant to be tongue-in-cheek.
There are three stages: a heart transplant, a kidney transplat, and a brain transplant (though, really, shouldn't it be called a "body" transplant?). After completing these stages, you repeat them in an ambulance which ups the difficulty. After you complete these in an ambulance, you repeat them again in space, which ups the difficulty a bit more. Late in the game there are a few bonus surgeries you can do on an alien, but I didn't have the patience to get this far.
The main challenge of the game is mastering the awful controls, and there isn't much more to the gameplay besides that. Sure, there are some easter eggs to find, and the over-the-top ridiculousness of game keeps it from being too boring. But, still, I can't imagine most people bothering to play this for more than a few hours tops. So if can you get this game inexpensively, it is good for a cheap laugh. Other than that, it's not really worth playing.

"Don't Tax Me, Bro!" tells the tale of a suave 80s dude-type who seems to find himself constantly on the run from the law. There is little explanation as to why our unnamed protagonist finds himself in this situation, but based on the title of the game, we are led to believe that he has not been paying his taxes.
The game begins with the manly man stood in what I presume is his place of residence. He's holding a briefcase and appears to be expecting a knock at the door at any moment. The door is then burst in and two police officers appear. The protagonist then darts over the balcony and begins running with no intention of stopping. While running from the dibble there are coins to collect, which can be used later in the game.
There are a variety of obstacles along the way which almost seem like they want to stop you in your efforts to escape the filth, who relentlessly pursue you the whole way. You will need to dodge plant pots, manholes, vicious dogs, and flying birds to but name a few. While the obstacles are plentiful, there is also assistance available along the way. This support comes in the form of power-ups such as a cup of coffee, which gives you a burst of energy to increase the distance between yourself and the fuzz; a vacuum cleaner, which picks up all the coins in your view; an explosive canister, which can be dropped on the plod; and an 80s-style mobile phone, which you use to call on two friends to run alongside you and take a hit from the many obstacles for you.
After running a few missions with our main man it is possible to spend some of your hard-earnt coin and request the support his fellow ethical tax-dodging associates who will run missions and collect coin for you. It seems there are people from all walks of life who recognise the truth that taxation is theft, and are willing to resist the state's attempts to collect taxes. You can also use the coins to buy fancy new items of clothing for your geezer.
All in all, a fun gaming experience, and a great message for all.

Alright, this game is getting some backlash for microtransactions. Whatever, it's buying Cosmetics, and I don't see you screaming at Valve about keys and crates.
Now this game has pros and cons like any other
Multiplayer is currently disabled. It is April 15th 2015 at the time of this Review, so that might change by the time you read this. Much like everything else in this review.
It's ragdolls are pretty good, however sometimes you get stuck through nets or your head rolls around like an owl turning it at mach 2.
The Terrain is b-e-a-utiful. The snow isn't just some all white texture on the ground. It seems like it in the sunlight for the most part, but you see some shiny specks here and there, but when you remove sunlight, say you get under a tree , you see the discrepancies in the snow, which are done perfectly. You also leave a trail in the snow, and it looks like flattened down snow, not just parted snow. The lakes and rivers are all frozen over and you can ski on them, but if you fall from serious height onto it you eat it, so I'll allow it.
One thing this game gives you is some serious fall height. It's pretty fun, and I've seen some crazy drops in the X-Games and things like that, but I just don't know. Maybe someone with some actual skiing experience can elaborate on that one.
The soundtrack is pretty good. Im personally not a fan of that kind of music, but it's like a kind of trance music, I guess? It's really soothing, and fits the game perfectly, so you're immersed immediately, even if you don't like it.  It also tells you the song name when it changes.
All in all, I only have three issues with the game. The standing animation (When you aren't moving) is a bit, I don't know, stiff? It doesn't seem life-like. It seems a bit rushed, I mean, if I moved my body like that to stretch I think I'd pull something. Perhaps it should be a bit slower, smoother and more natural. It's unnatural.
Issue Three is that when you go into an area, it says @ui_AreaName. Once that gets changed to just AreaName popping up on the screen it will blend perfectly.
My third issue is that the game doesn't save my sound settings. I turn the music off to talk to my friends or so I can listen to different music while I play, and every time I quit and come back, the music is back on. However, when I go into the settings, the slider is still set to off.
Now for my wishes and wants, these are things the game lacks, but I don't really see them as issues. I can live without them.
I wish it had some AI going around to fill the world a bit, and shops and such in the actual world to make use of the buildings you've made.
I wouldn't mind some dismounted mode either, where you can just walk around. It can be a pain to try to find a spot you want to drop in from if you ski uphill from your starting point.
I wish the ski lifts would actually let you hop on and ride them.
Outside of that, this game is looking very good, and with more improvements you're looking at what could set some future standards.

Negatives:

Conclusion:
Don't waste your time now, wait till it comes out to full version.

I'd played this game back when it was originally released by Sony - purchased the Collector's Edition.  Played it for a while, but since there was little to no content for level 30 people my wife and I moved on to other games before too long.
I'd completely forgotten about the game until seeing a reference to it again recently so I decided to give it a shot once more.  My advice is if you think you might be interested, try it on the month-to-month $15 subscription to try all the content/powers before spending any extra money on the content they are selling on Steam.  The Subscription price grants you access to *all* of the content they sell here, so if you wind up not being interested in the game it will save you quite a bit of money.  If you wind up getting reeled in, you probably want to subscribe anyway due to all the extras they give you beyond the other content (unlock keys, additional character slots, etc), so I'm not sure why you'd even buy the the content here -- but maybe that's just me.
The Pay-To-Win factor is just too high for me in general (it's just insanely expensive) along with lack of actual content, poor population of lower to mid tiers (CR110 and below), etc etc.  If I wanted solo content, there are *much* better games out there.
The short version is - nothing much has really changed since I played back at release.  I guess I'll check back in another 5-6 years from now (assuming they survive -- kinda doubt it) to see if they have improved at all yet.  City of Heroes was a better game really (it closed up shop in 2012) --  it just lacked the big industry "DC comics" name and characters, which is the only reason I can see that this game even still exists.
Give it a miss.  You'll save yourself a headache.

I've been a casual DCUO player since it came out. My favorite parts are early in the game as there is a LOT of options to customize your character at the beginning and even more while playing. You can easily spend and hour or more in character creation if you really like to have full control on your look. (there are shortcuts if you just want to get into the action) Now I'm writing this  review because I have a new PC and this time I installed it through stream (Maybe their rotating discounts can save me $ if I purchase DLCs in the future). I have a lot of play time in so don't go by my time on steam. I am mainly writing this because of the new stats revamp. If you're a new player then you won't know the difference. Get your superhero on as this is still one of if not the best Superhero MMOs around. Now I know why the hardcore players hate the stats revamp. There was a lot of work to get your stats the way you wanted them back in the old system and now a lot of that work has be streamlined in such a way that hours days and months of work are kinda out the window. Hardcore players of every game HATE total revamps. So let me give you my impression after logging back in and playing for a bit. The base game is the same. The way you fight, the look, the missions, the iconic characters etc are all there. If this game were being launched now for the 1st time everyone would love it (minus the slightly dated graphics). But when you spend so much time of your life on something change is hard to deal with. This change for DCUO isn't great. It's kind of a step sideways but its understandable. It makes it slightly easier for new players and yeah slaps the faces of old players a bit but not as bad as people are crying about in all the latest reviews.
Now here's my opinion. Get on Play it and have fun. It's free (at first) but can quickly suck lots of $ from you if you really get into it. If you're the type that character creation, solo play and replay is your thing you'll probably never spend $1. Character creation is very fun. And with several base types of characters you can play levels 1-30 over and over with different feels each time. If you're a group player it's easy to jump onto a team for group missions. Now here's the tough part. If you're a completionist or really in it for the long haul (like playing for years) then you'll end up spending money. No way around it as the game is kinda set up like a comic book series and after the first main storyline you'll have to pay for the more advanced stories. This also forces you to buy them if you want your character to keep growing. Don't worry though if you're even semi casual as it will be a while to get that powerful if you play through the game without any level skips. If you're new or were casual but stopped for a while get on this.

In the early stages of the game this problem is hampered by wood shortages so you cannot build ladders to prevent it or food tables, beds and a shelter to even heal them back up after. In the late game this problem results in spending significant amounts of time shoring up the map to stop the little morons killing themselves doing pointless things. Both are annoying.

People that know me know that I (perhaps to a fault) have rose tinted glasses when it comes to most things, especially artsy indie-ish things. It pains me to say that, definitively, there is no way in hell this deserves a 90 on metacritic and I felt very misled in my expectations, which is why I feel the need to compensate with a harsh review. While Brothers is a decent enough game, it is not 'Game of the Year' material. Remember, this is the game that BEAT OUT GTA5, Bioshock Infinite and Tomb Raider at the VGX. It boggles the mind.  Any themes it treads have been done much better elsewhere, and the novel puzzling mechanics, while somewhat interesting, are few and far between and often recycled one after another in sequence. I kept waiting for it to heat up, but the big kick never came.
I was led to believe there would be an intensely emotional story, and it was clear that the game was really reaching to provide one. The key ingredient in stories involving loss is that you have a connection to the characters involved. When none of them speak a line of meaningful dialog, that raises the bar significantly and puts the burden on the development of the actors through their actions. A good movie can take us inside the hearts of a fictional character and experience their sense of profound loss within 2 hours. Brothers had three and a half to get the job done, but never bothered to attempt to pick up the slack at all. Any acting done by any of the characters in the game is limited to simple pantomime, or broadly simplistic generalities. There are no facial expressions to appreciate, there are no meaningful challenges of character, there aren't even any gameplay choices that would write in some of the blanks yourself. So to compensate for any true connection to the characters, every 'emotional' scene is accompanied by a haunting soundtrack with string instruments and a lady chanting "ehhhhhhhh oooh ehhhhhhhhhh OOOOO", which sure IS KIND OF NICE (Don't get me wrong), but it's the equivalent of the "Applause" sign coming on for an audience and awkward in how hard it tries to manipulate you. It boils down to cartoonish looking characters crying while you sit in your seat feeling embarrassed for the game. I was so very disappointed.
The mechanic of using both sticks to control each character did shine through in a few instances. When the brothers tether themselves together with a rope and use it to navigate treacherous ruins, it seemed as though it was finally getting into its stride. The tutorial levels were over! And now it could begin in earnest! Then the game ended. Whoops.
The visuals were decent, but nothing extraordinary, however the character animations were poor. You know how in games when NPCs sleep, they sleep on top of the beds because no one wants to take on the complex task of "sheet physics". Well in this game, the father spends the entire game doing the same writhing & moaning animation (On a 5 second loop) while lying for days on top of a kitchen table. The artists couldn't even be bothered to draw a bed. Or even a pillow. Come on!
So did I like Brothers? Yes, I liked it. There are some interesting parts. Maybe even some good parts. But I did not love it.

My Review for: Parkitect - Right in the Childhood Edition.
Disclaimer: Played loads of the Humble version of the game.
The GOOD:
-If Planet Coaster is Roller Coaster Tycoon 4, this is 2.5.
-Nice colorful artstyle with the isometric camera angle that brings you back to the old RCT days...
-...but can be played in a full 3D mode or even in 1st person with mods!
-Did i mention MODS?!?!
-Workshop support, what RCT 3 so desparately needed in its heyday.
-Little changes like how shops need to be stocked up, the really cool black and white heat maps or the much better blueprint system are a really nice touch.
-(So Far) A decent selection of rides and they just added Transport Rides.
The MEH:
-Can't make my Boomerang or Montezoomas Revenge yet...no Launched Starts or backwards track creation yet :(
-Management stuff is not quite there yet, more sandboxy at the moment.
-No scenarios or campaign (yet).
Overall:
If new school high tech park management is your bag, Planet Coaster is the one to look out for. BUT, if you're like me and grew up with RCT 1-2, this is by far the better game. Texel Raptor have done an incredible job of bringing back my old childhood game and even in its Early Access state, its already leagues ahead of RCT World, and its only going to get better and better.

Parkitect is a Theme Park simualtion Game. It is inspired by RCT 1 and 2, but does so many stuff much better already than RCT2. First the visual improvement is a welcome change, much more accpetable by today's standard. There is great charm in the game also, watching people walk around adn see their travel logs is very gratifying. But by far the best aspect to this game in my opinion is the greatly improved coaster designer.
the coaster designer is not node based like planet Coaster, No limits or RCTW. Instead it's base on the RCT coaster designer, but it is so much better and allows for a lot of freedom. You can bank anyttime you want pretty much, you can extend and reduce track segments, it allows for a lot of smooth ride creation.
The biggest drawback for the game, is the lack of a tyccon at the moment. While you can make a profit on the park, the game still lacks some of the simualtion elements. For example the resource system is still a WIp which can drag down your park, but the system is worked on and the devs said they want to focus on that this month. The game also lacks some classic rides from RCT (Dingy slide, go karts, LIM coaster) and scenarios. For now its just sandbox.
The devs are great! They keep us updated every week with a blog post. They have not missed a single week post for 95 updates (They might have some days delay, but always up!). They updated the pre alpha every month, and I have complete confidence that they will not abandon this game at all!
There already is a modding community, which can enhance the game alot. Extra ride,s extra coaster types, extra scenery objects! Coaster Cam! I really recommend using it, it is very neatly integrated inside the game!
Thus, I say Parkitect is a must have if you look for a building simulation game

Parkitect is a modern take on Rollercoaster 1 and 2. Even though it is in early access and soon will be entering beta, the game feels very complete and you can already build the park of your dreams!
Most important changes that the game currently has:
- A better rollercoaster builder with a lot of freedom like track length and freeform banking. This means you can bank to any angle you want and resize track pieces to perfectly fit your requirements.
- Multiple visualization overlays so you can easily manage your park and create rides. - Advanced guest scenery interaction
- Resizable grid so you can place scenery everywhere you want inside the grid tiles themselves
- Mod support (Steam workshop and third party)
- Cute and playful graphics
- New and modern rides!
- Advanced scenario creator
- Easy ride and map sharing via blueprint images
- Sandbox mode
- Weekly development updates and monthly game updates
The game currently lacks:
- Backwards coaster building
- Undo button (ctrl-z)
- Ride music variety, only four songs are available of which 3 are similar
- Several coaster types (no shuttle, or multi-launch coasters)
- A campaign
Overall, already a great game that will only become better and better every update! So if you like Rollercoaster Tycoon 1 and 2, you will definitely like Parkitect!

I downloaded this game on a "free download" day and thus got this for free.
This game actually took me a little by surprise. Being quite the fan of platforming games this fit right up there.
Adding in there that this has multiple play modes and a build in co-op mode makes it even better!
The flow of this game lies a little higher then I am used too from other games so it might feel a bit fast when first starting out. But as far as controls go it feels smooth enough. Your character might do some weird jumps here and there when you are busy with wall jumping but It works pretty well. I myself played this with keyboard and got used to it pretty fast though I think people who not as keyboard heavy as me might prefer controller (which it of course supports)
The game uses a color switching mechanic that lets you navigate its many "bullet hell" puzzles. Although this is not a new thing this game does do this system justice in the way it implemented it.
This game has "2,5" game modes. There is the normal Story mode which follows your path through the world as you know it with some Voice over parts here and there. You have Arcade mode where you do a chapter up to the boss fight were speed is your aim. It has a score system if you wish to compete on leader boards and you have co-op mode.
Co-op mode is basically the solo story mode but with 2 players which is why I say it is a half mode. Certain points in the game are harder and some are easier with co-op but does not matter it is still fun to do. Now I do have to add that the game has specific co-op challenges that you and your friend can play through . They are special levels of 5 minutes a piece (there is like 5 of them) where a special thing is the focus for those 5 minutes. They are quite fun to do and recommended to test your friendship
I want to make a special note on how well made the boss fights are in my opinion. There are 5 bosses in the game and every single one of them is uniquely made for your current set of powers. If you fancy some good thought out fights in between your platforming then you will certainly enjoy these fights.
Its a fun platformer for both single as co-op play and added arcade mode for the optimize players and speedrunners. It has a nice difficulty curve but also a lot of checkpoints for people who are less comfortable with platformers letting everyone continue on in the story. I did not find any real negatives besides wall jumping is sometimes a little weird. And with that I mean that if you jump on a wall and don't do anything immediately you slide off. While falling down from a wall you can't really move anymore till you hit the ground making it that if you mis time a jump you can really recover at all times. But this is a really small thing in the whole package.
Would certainly recommend this for platform lovers or just something to do with a friend.

Brothers is an adventure puzzle game where you control two brothers with one controller. Of note, this game was designed to be played with a controller of some sort, I imagine they put PC controls in there by necessity of a PC release, but I guarantee the experience will be of substantially lower quality. The controls are simple but poignant, playing directly into the story being told. It is somewhat difficult to control both brothers at once, and you will inevitably find one of the brothers wandering off as you perform more immediate actions with the other, simulating, through gameplay, the flights of fancy the younger brother would be more prone to. Of course as you get more experience with it, you become more able to make the brothers work together, also following the story of the two brothers learning to rely on each other as you play, culminating in an emotional ending as their adventure nears its end. I loved this game, and beat it entirely in one sitting (I feel the story probably comes across best this way). It is fairly short at 3-4 hours long, depending on whether you try to find the small side quests scattered along the main quest line (I recommend you find and do these as they expand the story and relationship between the brothers), I found it engrossing the entire time. It is also gorgeous, a mixture of Disney animated stylization and....I would say norse mythology? Nearly every scene is framed in such a way as to be pleasing to look at, making the whole thing play out almost like an animated movie. I give it an A+, probably my second favorite game experience of 2013 next to The Swapper, entirely worth its $15 price tag (or cheaper, as it tends to go on sale fairly often).
Absolutely beautiful, engaging, unique, and emotional. A work of art in gaming. Maybe game of the year. Buy it, play it, be amazed.

Although Steam says Brothers requires a controller to play it doesn't, it has keyboard bindings - but there's no way you'd want to play it without a controller - so hopefully you have one. Sometimes the control scheme, which I've seen described as a novelty (a statement I don't agree with) can be confusing, I started to get used to it towards the end but at times it does remind you that it's there. The puzzles and game in general are probably too easy. Also, it ends.
There, I've covered literally all of the negative points I have about this game.
Clocking in at under 3 hours some people would say games like this are too short. These days I welcome games like this. It is excellent from start to finish. I did get it on sale, but it's worth full price in my opinion, without a doubt. I play plenty of multiplayer games or 60+ hour RPGs, now and then something comes along where it's a few hours of constant enjoyment. Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is exactly this. I had constant oldschool Sierra vibes from the artwork & atmosphere, something I have been begging for. It may be a lot of nostalgia, but it worked perfectly. Constant thoughts going back to the King's Quest, Gobliiins, etc. series.
I've seen a lot of people on forums make the argument that games can't tell a meaningful story or be considered art. While I couldn't stand or disagree with that statement more, I now have yet another game to point to. Not that those people probably give many games a chance, nevermind this one, but at least it's proof that they are wrong.
I have PSN+ and this will be free on it in a week or two. I thought about waiting, but I am glad I didn't. I wish I played this before New Years, as it would've been one of the three best games I played in 2013. I guess it will have to settle for being one of the best games I played in 2014.

Red Faction Guerrilla feels like a post apocalyptic game set on a distant future earth. No actually, its on mars. The game immediatley shoves the emphasis on fun and being able to destroy everything you see whilst gawping at the games great physics destruction effects. Literally, everything you see that isnt part of the terrian (i.e. cars, buildings, fences) can be destroyed using the various arsenal of weapons including explosive charges and your trusty sledgehammer. The story is nothing particularly exciting and
will follow. This game isn't based on giving you an intense, jaw dropping story based ecperience and has a pretty run-of-the-mill sotryline. The world is basically being held captive by an opressive evil government, your brother is part of the resistance group and he gets killed in pretty much the opening cutscene (the second one).
The characters that the game throws at you are pretty run of the mill, but that in no way ruins the experience of the game. It delivers satisfying destruction and fun gunplay and should not be ignored.
+ Great Destruction
+ Graphics are OK
+ Fun Gameplay
- Boring Story
- Un-interesting Characters
If you are looking for a story driven epic, just ignore this game. If you are looking to blow some stuff up and have a little bit of fun, then this game is probably a safe bet for you.

This is not your average game, this is an experience. An endurance test, to see how far you can go without failing and how much can you hold in your inner rage. This is a game which tries to find out what kind of a person you are, a game which tries to show you how cruel life can be. A game that has this much emotional depth is something unheared of, something magical and wonderful.
With a fantastic story about a man Diogenes getting stuck in a cauldron and using nothing but a sledgehammer to traverse obstacles, he is easily identified, with a quirky but wise attitude, he is determined to reach the end, no matter the cost. His facial expression adds to the immersion, showing true determination and patience throughout the adventure. Without a doubt, a character with plenty of personality, and one of the best characters in any form of media today.
Bennet Foddy, kindly provides quotes, both inspirational and thought provoking. Also, he helps you on the journey, by encouraging the player to tread forward, to the end of this odessey. His voice acting is superb, you can feel his emotions and expressions through his voice. Having a man like that by your side, you can't ask for anything more.
Accompanied with an amazing soundtrack that plays during gameplay, amazing level design that consists of various carefully placed props and objects, and thought provoking questions about man's existence and the purpose of life, this game is unlike anything that exists today. Having played this game, I can say it changed me for the better, having a diffirent perception towards life, and self redeeming qualities. A definite game of the year contender. Worth the eight euro asking price.
I wholeheartedly recommend this game.
